content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a new federated learning method named FEDCACU. The motivation is the empirical observation, that is, the knowledge shared from clusters of clients with low data heterogeneous to the clusters of clients with high data heterogeneous can significantly boost the latter’s personalized accuracy but not vice versa. To be precise, in the proposed method, the authors first cluster the clients based on their degree of data heterogeneity and then share the knowledge from the clusters with low data heterogeneous to the ones with high data heterogeneous during the whole training process. Some techniques for improving the communication efficiency are used. The authors conduct some experiments to evaluate the performance of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. This paper is well written and easy to read.

2. Some experiemntal results are interesting. For exmaple, the authors show that knowledge transfer during federated learning can be useful.

Weaknesses:

1. The authors make the conclusion, i.e., the knowledge shared from clusters of clients with low data heterogeneous to the clusters of clients with high data heterogeneous can significantly boost the latter’s personalized accuracy but not vice versa, from a toy experiment. The correctness of this conclusion is unclear. For example, in out-of-distribution learning, the recent studies show that the data from different environments can be used to eliminate the dependency of the final learned model on the spurious features. I understand the setting are a bit different.  But I still think there could be some knowledge transferring techniques, which transfer useful knowledge in the opposite direction as the authors have done. 

2. The setting of the proposed can be impractical in practice. For example, in the proposed method, all the clients should take part in the clustering process. The authors are recommended to develop a new clustering method to address this issue. 

3. In Proposition 1, the authors proved that CUAU can bounded by the earth mover’s distance (EMD). But how to understand from this proposition that CUAT can be (an accurate) measure of data heterogeneity?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is well written and easy to read. But the correctnesses of the idea and some claims in this paper are unclear.
content.summary_of_the_review: I recommend to reject this paper due to my comments above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper first makes the observation that the performance of highly non-iid clients benefit from the more iid clients, and not vice versa. Then, they proposed a technique called FEDCUAU that cluster the clients with different degrees of heterogeneity by leveraging the weight divergence. Due to privacy requirement, they measure the weight divergence between the client update and the global update. The clients are then clustered using the proposed measure. For communication efficiency, they performing clustering depending only on the weights of the last layers.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The paper demonstrates good writing. The idea of using knowledge from clients with different degrees of heterogeneity seems interesting.

Weaknesses:

(1) The observation that highly non-iid clients benefit from rather iid clients is not surprising, since the iid clients also contain data that are useful for the non-iid clients, and the training dataset distribution is more close to the actual test dataset. But the claim that iid clients do not benefit from non-iid ones is a bit hasty and unconvincing. How much heterogeneity is "highly" heterogeneous, which may harm the iid clients? If the threshold is set too low, it is possible that potentially useful clients are not adopted to help the iid clients.

(2) In terms of the design of algorithm, the paper seems to presume that all clients can participate in the clustering phase, which is not the case in reality. Interestingly, in the paper, a portion of clients are sampled in each round the later FL training phase, which is actually an effort to simulate this scenario.

(3) For the experiments, I find it quite unconvincing since the number of clusters are set to 2, so what if we have 50 perfectly iid clients, and 50 clients that are only a little bit non-iid, does this mean the iid clients are not benefiting from those other 50 clients? I think different number of clusters, as well as the heterogeneity in clients, are needed to illustrate the point.

(4) Regarding Table 4,  the corresponding baselines (without FedCUAU) are not shown, which is hard to know how much improvement FedCUAU really gives.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written, easy to understand. There is some novelty but limited. The paper does not provide code, but it should be rather easy to implement.
content.summary_of_the_review: I recommend rejection of this paper. since it has limited novelty and the experiments are not thorough.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper firstly studies how the different heterogeneity may affect the aggregated global single model. Then the authors propose a clustering algorithm to group clients based on the data heterogeneity. They also show the effectiveness of existing FL frameworks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The logic of this paper is sound and smooth. It is very interesting to explore the relationship between data heterogeneity and the single global model.
2. They cover most of the related works in this domain.
3. It is convincing to show the effectiveness by embedding the approach into existing pipelines.

Weakness:
1. From my understanding, dividing models into high level-layers and low-level layers is not a novel approach. 
2. For this kind of hard clustering algorithm, I am wondering if there is any guidance or discussion on how to select cluster numbers.
3. There are other federated clustering algorithms. I would suggest they can be added to the baselines to compare, such as IFCA[1] and FedSem[2].

[1] Ghosh, Avishek, et al. "An efficient framework for clustered federated learning." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (2020): 19586-19597.
[2] Xie, Ming, et al. "Multi-center federated learning." arXiv preprint arXiv:2005.01026 (2020).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-presented. The paper is a good preliminary work but may not reach the requirements of this conference considering the novelty. I am afraid I may not be able to fully reproduce the work given the current description.
content.summary_of_the_review: The research question itself is an interesting topic. The exploration and proposed approach are easy to follow. I am concerned about the comparison with other cluster-based federated learning baselines and the novelty.

content.title: FedCUAU: Clustered Federated Learning using weight divergence
content.TL;DR: This work uses the relative weight divergence between each client update and their aggregated update to cluster clients and govern the knowledge transfer between clusters to improve both the initial and personalized performance.
content.abstract: The majority of federated learning (FL) approaches aim to learn either a high-performing global model or multiple personalized models. Although there has been significant progress in each research direction, the optimization of one often comes at the expense of the other. In this work, we approach this problem by investigating how different clusters of clients with varying degrees of data heterogeneity may impact the single global model. From this empirical analysis, we discover a surprising insight: despite a significant distribution mismatch between clusters, the knowledge shared from low data heterogeneous clusters to high data heterogeneous clusters can significantly boost the latter's personalized accuracy but not vice versa. By building on this observation, we propose a cluster-based approach named FedCUAU, in which clients are clustered based on their degree of data heterogeneity, and knowledge between each cluster is selectively transferred. Experimental results on standard FL benchmarks show that FedCUAU can be plugged into existing FL algorithms to achieve considerable improvement both the initial and personalized performance. Empirical results shows that FedCUAU improves FedAvg initial global accuracy by $1.53\%$ and $1.82\%$ for Cifar10 and FEMNIST respectively, and personalized accuracy by $0.29\%$ and $3.81\%$.
